reuse.why: The range rule is put in a new getRangeAmount that getScheduledAmount also uses, but the server sites keep their own missing/number/range dispatch rather than calling the existing getScheduledAmount, which already handles all three cases.

duplication.why: No new copy of the range arithmetic, but the `null ? 0 : number ? v : range` dispatch remains repeated at the updateActions, postTransactionForSchedule, computeSchedulePreviewTransactions and normalizeSchedule sites beside a helper that already does it.

placement.why: getRangeAmount sits in shared/schedules.ts next to getScheduledAmount, the module that owns schedule amount logic.

scope.why: Only the range rule, its call sites, their comments, a focused test and a release note change.

maintainability.why: The rule now changes in one function, though two layers (getRangeAmount and getScheduledAmount) and the per-site dispatch remain for maintainers to keep aligned.

bypasses_abstraction.where: schedule-template.ts createScheduleList, forecast-schedules.ts normalizeSchedule, schedules/app.ts updateActions and postTransactionForSchedule, and computeSchedulePreviewTransactions resolve the amount themselves instead of calling getScheduledAmount.

disguised_duplication.where: Nothing duplicated is disguised; the remaining dispatch ternaries are pre-existing ones left in place.

one_place.where: The worst-case rule is defined once in getRangeAmount (shared/schedules.ts) and used by getScheduledAmount and every server site that previously computed the midpoint.
